1.pericope_label: The word to Zedekiah in the siege: thou shalt not escape, yet thou shalt die in peace with the burnings of thy fathers
debates: Why a sentence of capture is mixed with a promise of peace
Whether the burnings of the fathers mean cremation
Whether a violent death is worse than a lingering one
outliers: Clarke illustrates the burnings from funeral piles that consume the body, where Ellicott says flatly that the Hebrews never adopted cremation and embalmed their dead
Keil and Delitzsch reject the view of several scholars that these three chapters are appendixes, saying it accounts for neither their position nor their connection
themes: A prophecy that put its own author in prison
Eyes that behold a conqueror and are then put out
Mercy offered as an inducement to surrender
Burial argued as a token of the resurrection

6.pericope_label: Jeremiah spake all these words unto Zedekiah, while the army fought against Jerusalem, Lachish and Azekah
debates: What the naming of two surviving cities is meant to convey
Why these cities alone had not fallen
What it cost the prophet to deliver the message
outliers: Calvin reads the list of surviving cities as quiet ridicule of the confidence of Zedekiah, where Ellicott and Clarke treat it as plain topography
themes: A message delivered at the risk of the messenger life
Two names that mark how little was left
Fortification as the only reason for survival
Obstinacy read as a sign of a mind already gone

8.pericope_label: Zedekiah makes a covenant to proclaim liberty to the Hebrew servants, and the people turn and bring them back into subjection
debates: When this second prophecy was delivered
Whether the release was tied to the sabbatical year
What moved the people to reform and then to relapse
outliers: Clarke ties the manumission to the sabbatical year, and Gill answers that the sabbatical year released debts and not servants
Gill dates the relapse to the lifting of the siege, where Clarke dates it to the expiry of the seventh year
themes: A law kept in the book and not in the house
Freedom granted under pressure and withdrawn under relief
Preaching needed because the written word goes unread
Excuses that satisfy men and not God

12.pericope_label: I made a covenant with your fathers: ye turned and did right, and ye turned and polluted my name
debates: What at the end of seven years means when six years of service are named
Why a people just delivered from bondage were forbidden to hold it
Whether the brief obedience deserves praise or aggravates the crime
outliers: Calvin would have followed two versions in reading the seven years differently, and gives up that course only because the same words stand in two other places
Gill commends the people for turning from the ways of their fathers, where Calvin says the commendation is given only to show how detestable hypocrisy is
themes: A law grounded in the memory of slavery
No man a master who is not first free
Ears deliberately closed rather than merely dull
An oath sworn in the Temple and broken outside it

17.pericope_label: Behold, I proclaim a liberty for you to the sword: the men that cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts
debates: Whether the proclaimed liberty is granted to them or against them
Where the rite of the divided calf came from
What covenant is meant when God calls it his own
outliers: Calvin distinguishes the Roman rite, in which the victim was killed with a stone and not divided, from the eastern rite of cutting in two, where Ellicott adduces the Roman ceremony as a parallel to it
themes: A word of release turned into a sentence
Freedom from divine service described as bondage
An oath sworn between the halves of a victim
Signs given to wake men who will not attend

19.pericope_label: The princes and the eunuchs that passed between the parts of the calf: the army that is gone up from you shall return
debates: Whether the eunuchs named are literally such or a title of court officers
Why the sentence on Zedekiah is milder than on the princes
In what sense God commands an army that does not mean to obey him
outliers: Ellicott takes the eunuchs literally and traces their alien birth and court position, where Calvin denies that emasculated men are meant and makes the word a title of the chief men
themes: A judgment that names ranks so none may plead exemption
A besieging army withdrawn only to be recalled
Allies whose help was calculated for their own defence
Masters sentenced to the servitude they imposed
